synopsis: Stereo cameras estimate distance using two cameras with a known separation, while RGB-D cameras provide color and per-pixel distance; a wider stereo baseline improves long-range accuracy [f12595, f12596]. Fielded examples include Toyota SEnS+ (August 2021), which distinguishes people from objects using a rear stereo camera and slows a forklift by cutting power rather than braking, and John Deere SmartDetect Assist, which combines cameras, stereo and radar [f15785, f12598, f1654]. Simulation tools offer depth-camera capabilities through CARLA and NVIDIA Isaac Sim, but simulating flash or indirect time-of-flight cameras requires multipath and sensor-specific depth-noise models [f8468, f8478, f4603]. Camera depth is described as cheap, but stereo matching struggles on textureless surfaces, active depth-camera types have short range, and both retain general camera weaknesses [f12601, f12597]. No validation of camera-depth sensors for heavy-machine braking in dust or darkness was found, and Chapter 6 separately reports no public heavy-construction or mining automatic-braking validation evidence for flash or indirect time-of-flight depth cameras [f12602, f4604].
